question: For a Debian source package whose build demonstrably depends on the root path it is built in, does Hermit make the build independent of that path?
design: Prepare once, then build four times from the same prepared source in four DIFFERENT root paths: native in N1 and N2, hermit in A and B. Compare N1-vs-N2 and A-vs-B. The native pair is a per-package internal control establishing that the package really is root-sensitive, so a matching hermit pair is evidence about Hermit rather than about an already-reproducible package.
answer: 13 of 13 packages diverge natively across two roots; 13 of 13 are byte-identical under `hermit run --strict --no-rcb-time`. The control fired on every package, so no win is vacuous.
scope_warning: 13 packages with all four builds complete, selected as small fast-building members of the 8,688-name ASPLOS'20 target set. This is NOT a random sample and must not be reported as a percentage of that set. Selection is convenience-biased toward small packages.

hermit.branch: origin/main (clean checkout; binary reports g1fadc03779f2, no -dirty)
hermit.invocation_notes: The --bind is load-bearing: Hermit gives the guest a private /tmp tmpfs, so output under /tmp/drb-root would be discarded without it. Full namespaces retained; neither --no-namespace nor setarch -R is used.

reverie.state: unchanged by this experiment; the pin recorded by hermit 1fadc037

limitations: ARCH_SET_CPUID returns ENODEV: Hermit runs without CPUID interception

throughput.bottleneck: per-package prepare (apt build-deps + source download through a single serialized IPv6-loopback proxy bridge)

harness_repairs: rebuild.sh fetch-metadata: manifests are C-collation sorted but comm/sort honoured en_US.UTF-8, so verification refused with 'file 1 is not in sorted order'. Pinned both sides to LC_ALL=C.

container/finish-wheezy.sh: debootstrap --second-stage reinstates /usr/bin/ischroot itself and consumes the script's backup; the unguarded mv then failed and set -e aborted after the base system installed successfully, so the rootfs never got sources.list, policy-rc.d, or .drb-bootstrap-complete. Made the restore idempotent.
finish_bootstrap was unrecoverable after that failure: debootstrap deletes /debootstrap on success, and finish_bootstrap hard-required it. Both sides now accept an already-second-staged rootfs.
container_egress_recipe: fwdproxy is IPv6-only and unreachable from containers even with --network=host; an IPv4 loopback bridge fails with "Could not resolve '127.0.0.1'". Working: setsid ncat --listen ::1 13129 --keep-open --sh-exec 'ncat fwdproxy 8080'; DRB_CONTAINER_PROXY=http://[::1]:13129
not_attempted: dettrace oracle arm (additionally needs the modern-vDSO patch rebuilt)
confirmation of the confounder on a working-PMU host

results_summary.derivation: computed by ./summarize.sh from results.csv; not transcribed

timing_units_caveat: This experiment records no per-package durations, deliberately. Any duration printed by a build running under Hermit is VIRTUAL time (Hermit virtualizes the clock; a guest-side $SECONDS or `time` does not measure host wall clock). Approximate durations quoted in README.md are host wall-clock observed from outside the guest. Do not derive an overhead or slowdown factor from this experiment.
confounder: This host's PMU fails validation (AmdSpecLockMapShouldBeDisabled). Hermit derives virtual time from retired-conditional-branch counts, so without --no-rcb-time Hermit's own clock is a nondeterminism source. The default arm's six failures (figlet, grep, indent, nano, time, wdiff) all become IDENTICAL with --no-rcb-time and none of the seven passes changes -- the signature of a measurement artifact, not six product gaps. --no-rcb-time is REQUIRED for determinism measurement on this class of host.
retraction: An earlier version of this experiment described figlet/grep/indent/nano/time/wdiff as cases where Hermit's determinization is incomplete, and floated hermit#1850 (pipe readiness/EOF) as a possible cause of the figlet divergence. Both are withdrawn: figlet builds successfully and byte-identically under Hermit once virtual time is off the broken PMU, there is no hang, and nothing here supports a link to #1850.
